# LLMQuant research toolkit: repairing widespread misbehaviour without a test suite

A kit for gathering published scholarly writing, pulling it apart and asking a language model about it now misbehaves from almost every direction a user comes at it from. The repository has received 30 separate undocumented edits. Nothing about the outside services changed and nothing about the callers changed; the same things people did before come back wrong, and in several places something that used to be refused is quietly allowed, or something that used to be allowed is refused.

Bringing material in. Pasting a whole abstract-page address ending in /abs/2401.12345 no longer yields the identifier 2401.12345, and a downloadable address ending in /pdf/2401.12345v2.pdf no longer yields 2401.12345v2; for a full address nothing at all comes back. Asking the scholarly registry about an article gives its authors, journal, publisher, primary link and timezone-aware publication date exactly as expected, but the title comes back missing. Reading a syndication feed, in either of the two common XML dialects, goes badly wrong: when the elements sitting directly inside an entry are picked out by name, everything except the one asked for is kept, so titles, identifiers, links, timestamps and body HTML all come back wrong or absent.
